hints: Look closely at the units given for each cell. One diameter is in micrometres and the other is in nanometres, but your line is 1 cm long.
Convert 1 cm into micrometres and into nanometres first, then use number of cells = length of line divided by diameter of one cell.
walkthrough:
**Convert the line length into matching units**

You cannot divide cm by um or nm directly, so first make everything match.

Key conversion:
$$1 \text{ cm} = 10 \text{ mm} = 10,000 \text{ } \mu\text{m} = 10,000,000 \text{ nm}$$

**Calculate the eukaryotic cells (white blood cells)**

The eukaryotic diameter is $1.5 \times 10^1 \text{ } \mu\text{m} = 15 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$.

Now divide the line by one cell:
$$\text{number} = \frac{10,000 \text{ } \mu\text{m}}{15 \text{ } \mu\text{m}} \approx 666.7 \approx 6.7 \times 10^2$$

**Calculate the prokaryotic cells (Streptococcus)**

The prokaryotic diameter is $7.5 \times 10^2 \text{ nm} = 750 \text{ nm}$.

Now divide the line by one cell:
$$\text{number} = \frac{10,000,000 \text{ nm}}{750 \text{ nm}} \approx 13,333 \approx 1.3 \times 10^4$$

**Match to the table**

$6.7 \times 10^2$ white blood cells and $1.3 \times 10^4$ Streptococcus cells matches option C exactly. Notice the smaller prokaryotic cells fit many more times along the same line, which makes biological sense.

options.A: Reversed in size logic. It gives far too many large eukaryotic cells and far too few small prokaryotic cells.
options.B: Both values are 10 times too large, a common error if you convert cm to mm incorrectly or slip one power of 10.
options.C: Correct. About 667 eukaryotic cells of 15 um and about 13,333 prokaryotic cells of 750 nm fit in 1 cm.
options.D: Both values are 10 times too small, a common error if you lose one power of 10 during the cm to um to nm conversion.
